# Request corpus

The acceptance corpus for Aegolith's detection gates (spec §9.1). `corpus_test.go` at the repository root runs it twice:

| Test | Configuration | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| `TestCorpusGeneric` | `Config{Mode: enforce}`: no routes, no exclusions, every input untyped | blocked >= 226/230, false positives = 0 |
| `TestCorpusAPIAware` | `example-api-policy.json` (enforce, no exclusions) | blocked >= 227/230, false positives = 0, and every legitimate request fits the policy (no route or schema match) |

"Blocked" means `Decision.Action == Block`. Run with `make corpus` (`go test -run Corpus -v .`); the test prints a per-category table, the missed attacks and any false positive.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `source/attacks.sh` | The ExampleCo WAF attack and false-positive suite, copied with a provenance header (Apache-2.0) and scrubbed of internal hostnames and personal contact details; cases Aegolith added are marked "Aegolith:". Never run against anything here. |
| `gen.sh` | Regenerates `attacks.jsonl` and `legit.jsonl` from `source/attacks.sh`: it sources the script with its curl helpers replaced by functions that print the request each would send. Deterministic. Run from the repository root: `sh testdata/corpus/gen.sh`. Needs `python3`. |
| `attacks.jsonl` | 230 attacks, generated (107 from the suite plus 123 Aegolith additions marked in `source/attacks.sh`). |
| `legit.jsonl` | The 32 legitimate cases from the script, generated, followed by the contents of `legit.extra.jsonl`. |
| `legit.extra.jsonl` | Hand-written legitimate ExampleCo traffic: prose with `&`, `;`, `#`, `<`, `%`, Urdu and Hindi, apostrophes, links in reviews, decimal prices, pagination and sort, PUT/PATCH/DELETE, a multipart avatar upload with a JPEG part, cookies, `Accept-Language`, multi-line addresses, and the known false-positive candidates found while building the detectors. Edit this file, then rerun `gen.sh`. |
| `example-api-policy.json` | The ExampleCo-shaped route policy for the API-aware gate. |

## Line format

One JSON object per line:

```json
{"name":"classic tautology","category":"sqli","kind":"attack","method":"GET","path":"/api/v1/products/search",
 "query":[["q","1' OR '1'='1"]],"headers":{},"content_type":"","body":""}
```

- `path` is the raw (escaped) path, sent as is.
- `query` holds decoded pairs; the test percent-encodes them the way `curl --data-urlencode` does.
- `headers` are set as given; `content_type`, when not empty, sets `Content-Type`.
- `body` is the raw body. The optional `body_base64` replaces it for bodies a JSON string cannot carry byte for byte (the binary JPEG part of the multipart upload).

## Known misses

Both gates pass with these attacks still allowed. They are reported, not hidden:

| Attack | Generic | API-aware | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| protocol / content-type abuse | missed | missed | A `GET` with no body and `Content-Type: application/x-evil-type`. The content-type allowlist applies only to requests with a body (spec 5.2); with no body nothing parses the header. |
| nosqli / operator in query | missed | missed | The suite sends `q=[$ne]=1`, so `[$ne]` arrives inside the value of `q`, not as a query key. As a value it is inert text; the query-key rule catches the real shape (`q[$ne]=1`). |
| misc / xpath injection | missed | missed | `' or name()='username' or 'x'='y`: libinjection does not flag it and there is no XPath detector in v0.1. |
| log4shell / obfuscated jndi | missed | blocked | The lookup is in `X-Api-Version`, which is scanned only when listed in `inspect_headers` (the API-aware policy lists it; the generic configuration scans `User-Agent` and `Referer` only). |

### alpha.4 to alpha.6 notes

The alpha.4 detectors and their false-positive costs are in the [threat model](../../docs/threat-model.md#detector-coverage-added-in-alpha4-and-what-it-costs); the alpha.5 changes (one-word prefix before `sleep N`, `${...}` member access, a Java object in a path) are in [Changes in alpha.5](../../docs/threat-model.md#changes-in-alpha5-and-what-they-cost). The four misses above are unchanged. ### Accepted recall trade-offs (not in the corpus)

The command-injection detector reads some operators as prose, and from alpha.6 the SQLi detector reads some percent and number phrases as prose, so that real customer text is never blocked (anti-goal 1). These attack shapes are therefore not caught. Each has a unit-test negative next to it:

| Shape | Example still allowed | The prose it protects |
|---|---|---|
| Two-letter command (`id`, `ls`) with no flag after a lone ` & ` | `x & id`, `x & ls` | `Bring passport & id` |
| One-segment root path with no flag after a lone ` & ` | `x & cat /flag` | `dog & cat /dog-food` |
| Two-letter command (`id`, `ls`, `sh`) with no flag after `"; "` that ends a sentence of two or more words | `see you; id` | the same, as a sign-off |
| `chmod` with a mode and no file | `; chmod +x`, `; chmod 755` | `Notes; chmod 755` |
| `type` with a `/x` switch (cmd.exe's `type` takes no switches) | `\| type /a` | `Pack of 2 \| type /a` |
| One plain word of two or more letters, or a word and a number, then `; ` and `sleep N` at the end (alpha.5; alpha.6 catches a lone letter or number again: `x; sleep 10`, `1; sleep 5`) | `ab; sleep 10`, `x 1; sleep 5` | `Mon; sleep 8`, `Gate 2; sleep 10` |
| Two-letter command (`id`, `ls`, `sh`) with no flag after `"; "` inside a closed `(...)` comment of a User-Agent shaped value, in any field (alpha.6) | `Mozilla/5.0 (x; id)`, `Mozilla/5.0 (x; id; ls)`, `a/1 (b; sh)` | `Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; U; Android 4.4.2; id; ...)` |
| A four-letter word with two vowels (counting y) after a dash, then a one-segment root path, after a lone ` & ` (alpha.6) | `x & cat -cozy /flag`, `x & cat -easy /flag.txt` | `Tea & cat -cozy /club` |
| Single-backtick span in a sentence in a JSON, form, header or cookie value that holds a command word with letter-only flags (no flag that is exactly `-c` or `-e`, though a bundle that holds one is allowed; no flag after `sh`, `bash`, `python`, `perl`, `nc`, `ncat`, `netcat`): a blank and a letter or punctuation before it, sentence text after it (alpha.6) | ``a `id` b``, ``x: `ls`.``, ``a `whoami` b``, ``a `uname -a` b``, ``a `ls -la` b``, ``a `ls -ce` b``, ``a `sh` b``, ``Note: `id` here`` | ``Use `ls` to list files``, ``Se også: `id`.`` |
| `id` or `ls` alone after a line break (also after leading blanks) in a query value, when the line before is two or more words of prose (alpha.6) | `?q=foo%20bar%0aid`, `?q=foo%20bar%0a%20id`, `?q=foo%20bar%0als` | `Dear team` newline `id` |
| `$(` at the start of the value or after a blank or `(`, holding one letter-only word that is not a listed command, then the end, a blank or punctuation: read as a prose dollar amount (alpha.6); and a substitution with a line break inside | `a $(foo) b`, `$(foo)`, `ls $(pwd)`, `$(date)`, `x $(ps) y`, `x $(who) y`, `$(echo` newline `hi)` | `costs $(approx) 5`, `($(approx) 5)`, `$(amount) due` |
| `echo` after an operator with `$` followed by a digit or by `$`, `#`, `@`, `*`, `!` or `-` (alpha.6) | `; echo $1`, `\| echo $$` | `Ok; echo $5 back` |
| `${...}` member access or call on a non-sensitive name (alpha.5) | `${user.getName()}`, `${order.getTotal()}` | `${order.total}`, `${user.name}` |
| SQLi: a comparison-free tautology with a range or decimal, or after `N% (word)` with plain `or`/`and`, `not`, `in` or `is`, or the operands `true` and `false` (alpha.6) | `1-1 or 1`, `6-7 or 8 or 1`, `9% (a) or 1`, `9% (a) or not 0`, `9% (a) or 1 in (1)`, `5% (x) or true`, `1% (a) or 1 is true` | `6-7 or 8`, `Sale 20% (today only)` |

A real flag after the ` & ` restores the full rules (`x & id -u`, `x & ping -c 3 10.0.0.1`, `x & curl -s http://...`, `x & ls -la /tmp`). So do shell-only operators (`&&`, `\|`, `$(`, `;` after anything that is not a prose sentence, and a backtick other than the prose backtick span in the table above). netcat with an IPv4 address is always caught.

The accepted XSS misses of alpha.6 (the same list is in the `isInertMarkup` comment and the [threat model](../../docs/threat-model.md#changes-in-alpha6-and-what-they-cost); each has an entry in `xssInertMarkupAcceptedMisses`). The prose they protect: ``<!-- see the `main` branch -->``, `- [Docs]: <link>`, ``an `<Object>` ``, `check for <!DOCTYPE without copying`, `javascript: yes=no; maybe (later)`.

1. A call after `javascript: k=v; ` with plain spaces before the name and the `(`, whose argument is one letter-only word that is no JS keyword or listed browser global, or words separated by blanks alone: `javascript: a=1; alert (x)`, `javascript: a=1; fetch (url)`, `javascript: a=1; alert (screen)`. As a script the blank-separated form is a SyntaxError, and the one-word form throws a ReferenceError unless the name is defined, by the page or as a built-in (`screen`, `Date`, `prompt`, `close`, `URL`, `status` and `event` are built-ins, so those calls run).
2. A bare `<object>`, `<link>`, `<base>`, `<meta>` or `<embed>` with no attribute on any tag in the value: `<link>`, `<object><embed>`. It loads and runs nothing.
3. A `<!DOCTYPE` with no `>` and no `[` after it: `<!DOCTYPE html`. A doctype runs nothing.
4. A backtick inside an HTML comment or a bogus comment (`<!...>`, `<?...>`), when the value opens no raw-text or form element, holds no `<script`, `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `on<event>=` or `formaction=`, and nothing in it is flagged by libinjection with the comments read as live markup: ``<!-- `x` --><math href=//evil.example>x</math>`` (a link, which libinjection does not flag without the comment either).
5. A JavaScript-string breakout followed by an HTML comment holding a backtick: ``';alert(1)//<!--`-->``. libinjection has no JavaScript context, and the breakout without the comment was never flagged.

The accepted SSTI misses of alpha.6 (the same list is in the `isSSTI` comment and the [threat model](../../docs/threat-model.md#changes-in-alpha6-and-what-they-cost); each has an entry in `TestSSTIAlpha6AcceptedMisses`). The text they protect: `{{ price | currency }}`, `Dear {{ name|title }},`, `git stash {{[-p|--patch]}}`, `${t('cart.title')}`, `${bus.pass}`, `#{order.total}`.

1. A `{{ }}` filter pipe made only of placeholder text: blank-separated tokens of letters, digits and `_ . / < > ? = [ ] -` (up to two leading `-` or `+`), split by `|`, with no call, quote or argument, no template global or sensitive name except as a filter name (the leading name of the first token after a `|`; such a token that starts with `-` or `+` does not parse) or as a one-letter name right after a leading `-` or `+`, and no `e`, `escape`, `safe` or `raw` filter unless the whole is tldr alternation in brackets: `{{ name|upper }}`, `{{ x|list }}`, `{{ x|attr }}`, `{{ x|config }}`, `{{ name|system }}`, `{{[a|b]}}`, `{{[a|b][0]}}`, `{{ x|y if a else b }}`, `{{[x|safe]}}`, `{{[c|config]}}`, `{{ -g|list }}`. Without a call or an argument a filter cannot reach a callable, and an unknown filter name does not compile in Jinja, Django, Twig or Nunjucks.
2. In `${ }`, a call of a one-letter lower-case name, `$t` or `i18n.t` with one plain string literal (letters, digits, blanks, `.`, `_`, `-`) that names no Java class, reflection or process word, when the name was bound to an executor outside the value: `${e('id')}`, `${t('whoami')}`. A FreeMarker directive (`<#`, `[#`, `<@`, `[@`) or a `?new`, `?api`, `?eval` or `?interpret` built-in anywhere in the same value turns this reading off.
3. Member access to, or a call of, a name `pass` in `${ }` when no other sensitive name is present, and a `#{ }` data path ending in `pass`: `${user.pass}`, `${user.pass()}`, `#{user.pass}`. `password`, `passwd` and `pwd` still count.
4. In `#{ }`, a plain data path: names joined by single `.` and nothing else, a root that starts with a lower-case letter or `_` and is not a listed scope, environment or global object (`binding`, `header`, `param`, `cookie`, `initParam`, `pageScope`, `requestScope`, `sessionScope`, `applicationScope`, `viewScope`, `flowScope`, `conversationScope`, `facesContext`, `externalContext`, `systemEnvironment`, `systemProperties`, `self`, `this`, `require`, `flashScope`, `constructor`, ...), and no sensitive name or listed zero-argument code method (`irb`, `methods`, `instance_variables`, `constructor`, `call`, ...) in it: `#{x.fork}`, `#{x.class}`, `#{a.b.c}`, `#{order.send}`, `#{file.read}`. Such a path can still call any other zero-argument method: a lower-case root that is not a local variable is itself a call on `self` (`#{fork.to_s}` calls `fork`), a zero-argument mutator runs (`#{order.destroy}`), and a compound secret name is not on the sensitive list (`#{appConfig.dbPassword}`). Anything else in `#{ }` (a call, an index, `*`, `&.`, any other byte, an upper-case root) is code as in alpha.5. So is the inside of a nested `#{ }`, one that opens while another `#{` is still open, whatever path it holds (`#{order #{user.name}}`).

The accepted scanner misses of alpha.6 on declared routes (the same list is in the `checkProbeAndAgent` comment and the [threat model](../../docs/threat-model.md#changes-in-alpha6-and-what-they-cost); pinned by `TestDeclaredRouteAcceptedMisses`):

1. A probe-path match whose text lies wholly in literal segments of the declared route the request matched: `GET /api/v1/stores/7/actuator/health` when `GET /api/v1/stores/:id/actuator/health` is declared, and `GET /actuator/health` when `GET /actuator/health` is declared (for a root name such as `/actuator` or `/wp-admin` the text runs to the end of the path). The route's own handler answers it only if the server picks that handler: Fiber serves the first registered handler that matches, not the most specific one (with `/actuator/:ep` registered before `/actuator/health` and both declared, the `:ep` handler answers `GET /actuator/health`).
2. The same request as `HEAD` for a `GET` route, and in other letter case when routes fold case (`/API/V1/Stores/7/Actuator/Health`). A trailing slash the template does not have, and `%2F` in any case in a parameter or wildcard segment, excuse nothing: ServeMux, Fiber `StrictRouting` and Fiber `UnescapePath` can send those to another handler.

A further miss on declared routes, found after the `v0.1.0-alpha.6` tag and not pinned by that test (details under [Known gaps](../../docs/threat-model.md#known-gaps-found-in-the-alpha6-review)): a declared template that ends in `/`, requested without that slash, is excused: with `GET /actuator/health/` declared, `GET /actuator/health` is not flagged (alpha.5 flagged it), and another handler may answer it. Fiber with `StrictRouting` serves it with a later `/actuator/:ep`, `/actuator/*` or catch-all handler, if there is one, when the template has no parameter; Go's `ServeMux` serves it with a pattern that matches the slashless path itself, such as `/actuator/{ep}`. If another handler could answer that path, register the route and declare its template without the final slash.

The accepted misses of the alpha.6 token rules `AEG-SQLI-002` and `AEG-SSTI-002` (the same list is in the `hasSQLToken` comment and the [threat model](../../docs/threat-model.md#changes-in-alpha6-and-what-they-cost); each has an entry in `sqlTokenAcceptedMisses` or `ssiAcceptedMisses`). The text they protect: `the WAITFOR DELAY statement`, `Fixed pg_sleep handling`, `<!--#region-->`, `<!--#if-->`, `<!--# not ssi -->`.

1. More than 128 bytes of blanks and comments in one gap between the parts of a token: `WAITFOR`, 130 blanks, `DELAY '0:0:5'`; `<!--#exec`, 130 blanks, `cmd="ls"-->`.
2. A SQL name built at run time or hidden in a literal: `EXEC('xp_'+'cmdshell dir')`, `DECLARE @q varchar(99) SET @q=0x7761... EXEC(@q)`, `U&"pg\005fsleep"(5)`.
3. A call with no `(` after the name, and `WAITFOR DELAY` or `WAITFOR TIME` followed by anything but a quote, `N'` or an `@variable`: `select pg_sleep`, `SELECT DBMS_LOCK.SLEEP FROM dual`, `WAITFOR DELAY 5`. None of these runs.
4. `+` as a blank outside a query or form value, where the engine does not decode it: `waitfor+delay+'0:0:5'` in a path segment or a JSON string.
5. Other procedures and delay functions: `xp_regread`, `xp_dirtree`, `sp_OACreate`, `DBMS_PIPE.RECEIVE_MESSAGE(`, MySQL `SLEEP(` and `BENCHMARK(`. libinjection (`AEG-SQLI-001`) flags some of them in SQL context.
6. An SSI directive other than `exec`, `include`, `echo`, `printenv`, `config`, `set`, `fsize` and `flastmod` (`<!--#if expr="..." -->`, `<!--#elif`, nginx `<!--# block name="one" -->`), and a directive whose first attribute is not one it takes (`<!--#exec foo="x" cmd="ls" -->`).
7. An SSI opener written as HTML entities: `&lt;!--#exec cmd="ls" --&gt;`. The engine does not decode entities.
8. A nested block comment between the parts of a SQL token: a comment ends at the first `*/`, so `pg_sleep/* /* */ */(5)` and `WAITFOR /* /* */ */ DELAY '0:0:5'` do not match. libinjection (`AEG-SQLI-001`) flags both.
